***IMPORTANT FOR #BBA STUDENTS***
***APPLICABLE FROM #143 BATCH***
We people are confused about history, pol and pad courses. Biggest confusion is, which one do we need to complete or which one don't. So the answer is..........
From #Humanities section we have to complete 9 credit I mean 3 courses where Philosophy (PHI401) and Emergence of Bangladesh (HIS103) is mandatory. Now you have to choose/complete another 1 course from HIS101/HIS205.
So, total 9 credit I mean 3 courses are done from #Humanities section.
Now, you have to complete 6 credit I mean 2 courses from #Social_Science section where you have to choose any one from SOC101/GEO205/ANT101. So, 3 credit done.
#Note: If anyone done with SOC then no need to take GEO or ANT anymore or anyone done with GEO then no need to take SOC or ANT. If anyone takes that mistakenly then that will be considered as open elective course. Thats why dual major people should know this properly.
For another 3 credit you have to choose any one course from POL101/POL104/PAD201.
#Note: If anyone done with POL101 then no need to take POL104 or PAD201 anymore or done with PAD201 then no need to take POL104 or POL101. If anyone takes that mistakenly that will be counted as open elective course. Again dual major people should know about this properly.
So total 6 credit I mean 2 courses are done from #Social_Science section.
Don't ask anyone "Which one is easy between POL and PAD?." Think before ask it. Because you have to complete one course either POL or PAD. So, whoever is done with POL, he/she will say POL is easy because he/she doesn't complete PAD and vice-versa.

comments.text:
BBA students must take any two courses from HIS101, HIS102, HIS103, or HIS205.
However, many students often get confused about the content of these courses—what each course covers, which one is interesting, which one might be boring, etc. So, I am providing a detailed discussion on all four courses: HIS101, HIS102, HIS103, and HIS205. Hopefully, this will help you.
HIS101 – The title of this course is "History and Culture of Bangladesh."
The content of this course can be divided into several parts:
Ancient Archaeology of Bengal – In this section, you'll learn in detail about ancient archaeological sites of Bengal, such as Mahasthangarh, Paharpur, Mainamati, and Wari-Bateshwar.
Ancient and Medieval History of Bengal – This section covers the history of various kings and rulers of ancient and medieval Bengal, different regimes, and the lifestyle of that time. The course generally covers up to the period before the Battle of Plassey.
Culture of Bengal – This includes various cultural topics like Sufism, how Sufism spread in Bengal, the arrival of Islam, and traditional folk music of Bengal such as Lalon Fakir's songs and Baul music, along with celebrations like Pohela Boishakh.
Modern Social Reformers of Bengal – You will learn about social reformers from both Islamic and Hindu backgrounds in Bengal, such as Raja Rammohan Roy, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, Syed Ahmed Ali, and others.
HIS103 – The title of this course is "Emergence of Bangladesh."
This course starts from the Battle of Plassey and covers the entire British colonial period and the era of Pakistan. You will study in detail various movements and wars during these times. The course concludes with the Liberation War of Bangladesh.
HIS102 – The title of this course is "Introduction to World Civilization."
Unlike HIS101 and HIS103, which include historical topics you might have studied during school, most of the content in HIS102 and HIS205 is likely to be new for many students.
In HIS102, you will first learn about ancient civilizations of the world. These include the Egyptian civilization, Mesopotamian civilization, Indus Valley civilization, Vedic period, Chinese civilization, Hebrew civilization, Persian civilization, Arab civilization, Greek civilization, Roman civilization, and the Mayan civilization. You’ll explore their histories, how these civilizations developed, and their contributions to the world.
The course then moves into early modern history, covering important topics like the Renaissance and the Industrial Revolution. Additionally, you’ll learn about major world religions, including Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, Confucianism, Islam, Zoroastrianism, Christianity, and Judaism.
HIS205 – The title of this course is "World History."
This course mainly focuses on modern world history. HIS205 essentially picks up where HIS102 ends. It begins with the Renaissance and the Industrial Revolution and then moves on to topics such as the French Revolution, World War I and World War II, the division of Germany, the Cold War, and other significant global historical events of recent centuries.
So, this was an overview of the main content of all four courses. Now it's your decision—which two courses will you choose?
The course content is summarized by,

text:
BBA students must take any two courses from HIS101, HIS102, HIS103, or HIS205.
However, many students often get confused about the content of these courses—what each course covers, which one is interesting, which one might be boring, etc. So, I am providing a detailed discussion on all four courses: HIS101, HIS102, HIS103, and HIS205. Hopefully, this will help you.
HIS101 – The title of this course is "History and Culture of Bangladesh."
The content of this course can be divided into several parts:
Ancient Archaeology of Bengal – In this section, you'll learn in detail about ancient archaeological sites of Bengal, such as Mahasthangarh, Paharpur, Mainamati, and Wari-Bateshwar.
Ancient and Medieval History of Bengal – This section covers the history of various kings and rulers of ancient and medieval Bengal, different regimes, and the lifestyle of that time. The course generally covers up to the period before the Battle of Plassey.
Culture of Bengal – This includes various cultural topics like Sufism, how Sufism spread in Bengal, the arrival of Islam, and traditional folk music of Bengal such as Lalon Fakir's songs and Baul music, along with celebrations like Pohela Boishakh.
Modern Social Reformers of Bengal – You will learn about social reformers from both Islamic and Hindu backgrounds in Bengal, such as Raja Rammohan Roy, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, Syed Ahmed Ali, and others.
HIS103 – The title of this course is "Emergence of Bangladesh."
This course starts from the Battle of Plassey and covers the entire British colonial period and the era of Pakistan. You will study in detail various movements and wars during these times. The course concludes with the Liberation War of Bangladesh. 
HIS102 – The title of this course is "Introduction to World Civilization."
Unlike HIS101 and HIS103, which include historical topics you might have studied during school, most of the content in HIS102 and HIS205 is likely to be new for many students.
In HIS102, you will first learn about ancient civilizations of the world. These include the Egyptian civilization, Mesopotamian civilization, Indus Valley civilization, Vedic period, Chinese civilization, Hebrew civilization, Persian civilization, Arab civilization, Greek civilization, Roman civilization, and the Mayan civilization. You’ll explore their histories, how these civilizations developed, and their contributions to the world.
The course then moves into early modern history, covering important topics like the Renaissance and the Industrial Revolution. Additionally, you’ll learn about major world religions, including Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, Confucianism, Islam, Zoroastrianism, Christianity, and Judaism.
HIS205 – The title of this course is "World History."
This course mainly focuses on modern world history. HIS205 essentially picks up where HIS102 ends. It begins with the Renaissance and the Industrial Revolution and then moves on to topics such as the French Revolution, World War I and World War II, the division of Germany, the Cold War, and other significant global historical events of recent centuries.
So, this was an overview of the main content of all four courses. Now it's your decision—which two courses will you choose?

BEN205 has been made an optional course along with other language courses. This means, now you have the following mandatory courses, i.e., ENG102 (if not waived), ENG103, ENG105, and you need to complete any one from BEN205, CHN101, and ENG115. See the following table:
1. ENG102 [Mandatory if you donot get weived]. 
2. ENG103 [Mandatory ].
3. ENG105 [Mandatory ].
4. BEN205/CHN101/ENG115 (Choose any one).
2. GED Humanities Courses (3 courses / 9 credits):
HIS103 has been made an optional course along with other HIS courses. This means, now you have one mandatory course, i.e., PHI401, and you need to complete any two from HIS101, HIS102, HIS103, and HIS205. See the following table:
1. HIS101/HIS102/HIS103/HIS205 [Any two]. 
2. PHI401 [Mandatory].
3: GED Science Lab Courses:
The 1-credit lab courses, i.e., BIO103L, ENV107L, PBH101L, PSY101L, PHY101L, and CHE101L, have been made optional. Students who wish not to take lab courses can take one 3-credit course of their choice from any other Department/School apart from BBA, as 'Free/Open Elective'. Students who have already completed one or two lab courses are advised to take the 
remaining lab course(s) to fulfil their credit requirement. 
4. BUS498 Internship or Research Project:
4 credits of BUS498 Internship will be counted towards CGPA, effective Spring 2025. From Summer 2025, BUS498 will be titled as 'Internship and Research Project'. This will allow students to take a research project as an alternative of internship. However, a student must have a CGPA 3.30 in order to take the research project. Students are allowed to take one extra course with BUS498.

★143 batch & onwards যারা কোনো lab করেন নাই তাদের history থেকে আর একটি course করার কথা বলা হয়েছে। এক্ষেত্রে His103 করা বুদ্ধিমানের কাজ।তবে মনে রাখবেন His103,এই course টি 143 batch & onwards দের জন্য Mandatory নয়। কিন্তু History থেকে যেহেতু 3টি course করতে হচ্ছে তাই আপনি his101/his102/his205 এই 3টির মাঝে যেকোনো 2টি এবং his103 করে রাখতে পারেন।
★143 batch & onwards যারা একটি/দুইটি lab করে ফেলেছেন, তাদের lab 3টি করে ফেলাই সবচেয়ে নিরাপদ। মনে রাখবেন যারা 3টি lab course করছেন তাদের history course নিয়ে কোনো ঝামেলা পোহাতে হবেনা। তাই আপনার যদি lab course করা থাকে তবে বাকি lab গুলো complete করে ফেলুন। 
★143batch & onwards যারা lab করেন নাই এবং his103 ছাড়াই অলরেডি history থেকে 3টি course করে ফেলেছেন, তাদের নতুন করে his103 করতে হবেনা।
★163batch & onwards যারা আছেন his103 তাদের জন্য Mandatory course এবং সকলকে অবশ্যই এই course করতে হবে।এছাড়াও history থেকে বাকি যে 3টি course(his101,his102,his205) রয়েছে সেখান থেকে 2টি course করতে হবে। See less
